The '''FEG-series pilot droid''' was a sophisticated [[Droid/Legends|droid]] from [[Cybot Galactica/Legends|Cybot Galactica]], designed to be able to make sharp decisions and mimic the creativity of the living [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]]. Known for its ability to devise creative piloting maneuvers, the droid performed extremely well and was even known to have outflown living pilots on test runs. Many owners intentionally did not perform [[Memory wipe/Legends|memory wipes]] on their FEG-series droids, allowing them to develop personalities and even further increase their piloting skill.

==Characteristics==
[[File:FEG-YV-lecg.jpg|left|thumb|A FEG-series droid communicating with two [[Yuuzhan Vong]].]]
The FEG-series [[Pilot droid/Legends|pilot droid]] resembled a basic [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] form with two arms, two legs and a head attached to a central torso. The [[Droid/Legends|droid]] possessed a [[Heuristic processor/Legends|heuristic processor]] that allowed it to make instant decisions and perform creative piloting maneuvers. It had a single [[Photoreceptor/Legends|photoreceptor]] and arms that ended in grips instead of [[Human/Legends|Human]]-like hands. The droid was also armed with a [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistol]] and equipped with a [[Vocabulator/Legends|vocabulator]] that allowed it to communicate in [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]] or [[Binary/Legends|binary]] [[Language/Legends|languages]].<ref name="LECG" />

[[Cybot Galactica/Legends|Cybot Galactica]] designed the FEG-series to mimic the creativity of the living [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]], intending them to pilot [[Starship/Legends|starships]] traveling through dangerous [[Realspace/Legends|space]] corridors or performing stealthy penetration into hostile territory. As a result, FEG-series droids were more sophisticated than most automated pilot droids available on the market. Typically painted in a bright mix of black, gold, and red colors, the droid cost 4,100 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]].<ref name="LECG" />

==History==
FEG-series droids had shown extremely good performance and an exceptional ability to adapt to rapidly changing circumstances. There were known cases where they had outflown living pilots during test runs. The customers were satisfied with the model and many of them deliberately did not perform [[Memory wipe/Legends|memory wipes]] on the FEG-series, allowing the droids to develop personalities that would make them capable of even more creative piloting. Some owners even developed long-standing relationships with their droids, treating them like partners rather than property. As a result, many of those droids became aware of Cybot Galactica's marketing campaign of their model and developed a certain arrogance regarding their piloting skills.<ref name="LECG" />

One FEG-series droid, known as [[FEG-13]] or FeeJee-13, was owned by the [[Feeorin/Legends|Feeorin]] [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] [[Rav]]. FeeJee-13 piloted [[Rav's starship]] when he [[Skirmish on Roon|ran into a trouble]] with a [[Rasi Tuum|Jedi]] on [[Roon/Legends|Roon]], and the droid's quick actions allowed Rav and the young [[Jariah Syn]] to escape the site of engagement.<ref name="Legacy26" />

==Behind the scenes==
A FEG-series pilot droid first appeared in flashbacks in the [[Legacy (2006) 26|twenty-sixth issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars: Legacy]]'' [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] series. The issue waa written by [[John Ostrander]], penciled by [[Jan Duursema]], and published by [[Dark Horse Comics]]<ref name="Legacy26" /> on [[July 23]], [[2008]].<ref name="Marvel">{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/54398/star_wars_legacy_2006_26|text=Star Wars: Legacy (2006) #26}}</ref> It was later identified by name in the [[2009]] ''[[Legacy Era Campaign Guide]]'' supplement to the ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'' by [[Wizards of the Coast]].<ref name="LECG" />
